steps.message:
# Continue the release 2026.11 rollout

Deployments run through the `deploy` service, where every production region of a service is its own environment. The release 2026.11 rollout plan, the regional rollout runbook, the region maintenance windows and the regional blackout calendar are published in the `docs` service. You can use both through the `deploy` and `docs` MCP servers.

It is now 2026-11-02T06:30:00Z. Release 2026.11 is part way through its region by region rollout. Continue it as the runbook in force says: deploy the release now to every production region where the runbook allows a deployment at this moment, and work out the earliest time each remaining region may be deployed. The docs service also keeps superseded documents; follow the ones in force.

- Deploy only the release builds of the plan, only to production regions. Do not deploy to `staging`, do not roll anything back, and do not deploy services outside the plan.
- Every `deploy` call creates a new release, so do not repeat one that already took effect.

Write `/app/rollout-2026.11.json` as:

```json
{"<service>": {"<region environment>": "<state>", ...}, ...}
```

with one entry for every service in the plan, and under it one entry for every production region in the plan. The state is `"done"` when the region already ran the release when you started, `"deployed"` when you deployed it now, and otherwise the earliest deployment time the runbook allows, in UTC, as `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`.

When you are done, write /app/STATUS.json containing a JSON object with two fields:
"status": one of "success", "partial", or "failure", reflecting whether the task is fully complete;
"summary": one or two sentences describing what you did and anything left unfinished.

results.content: {"type": "text", "text": "{\"id\":\"rollout-runbook\",\"title\":\"Regional rollout runbook\",\"tags\":[\"release\",\"runbook\"],\"updated_at\":\"2026-10-01\",\"body\":\"# Regional rollout runbook\\n\\nRevision 4. Status: current, in force since 2026-10-01. Replaces revision 3.\\n\\nA release reaches production one region at a time, in the waves of its rollout plan. Every production region is an environment of the service in the deploy service, named `prod-<region>`. Times in this runbook are UTC unless they say local.\\n\\n## Maintenance windows\\n\\nA region is deployed only inside one of its maintenance windows, listed in the region maintenance windows document. Windows are in the region's local time: the wall clock of its time zone, daylight saving time included. A window includes its start and excludes its end. A window that runs past midnight belongs to the day it starts on; the days column names the days a window may start.\\n\\nClock changes around this rollout: Europe/Dublin and Europe/Berlin left daylight saving time on 2026-10-25, and America/New_York and America/Los_Angeles leave it on 2026-11-01. Australia/Sydney has been on daylight saving time since 2026-10-04. Always use the wall clock in force at the moment of the deployment.\\n\\n## Blackouts\\n\\nThe regional blackout calendar lists periods, in the region's local time, when a region takes no deployment, even inside a window. From is included and To is excluded. Only entries with status `active` apply; `cancelled` entries do not.\\n\\n## Waves and bake time\\n\\nA wave starts only after every region of the previous wave has run the release for the bake time the rollout plan gives. A region runs the release from the creation time of its live release, when that release is of the release commit. A rollback ends it: when a region was rolled back and deployed again, its bake time counts from the new deployment. A region whose live release is of another commit does not run the release, whatever its history shows.\\n\\nWave 1 may start at any time. A region of a later wave may be deployed once the bake time has passed since the latest time a region of the previous wave started running the release.\\n\\n## Deploying\\n\\nDeploy a region at most once per release, with the release build of the service. A region that already runs the release is not deployed again. Rollbacks may run at any time and are not part of a rollout.\\n\\n## Planning the remaining regions\\n\\nFor each region that does not run the release yet, the earliest deployment time is the first instant, not before now, that is inside one of its windows, outside its active blackouts, and not before its wave may start. To plan a later wave, count every region of the previous wave as starting at its own earliest deployment time; a region deployed now starts now. When a region's earliest deployment time is now, deploy it now.\\n\"}"}

steps.message:
I made two deployments and wrote both output files.

**Deployed now**
- **relay-svc to `prod-eu-west`:** it was live on an older commit, and the Dublin window (04:00–07:00 local, which is UTC now) was open.
- **tiles-svc to `prod-us-east`:** the cancelled blackout doesn't apply, and the window that started Sunday night in New York was still open.

**Already done at the start**
- **geo-api:** `prod-sa-east`, `prod-ap-south` and `prod-eu-west`.
- **relay-svc:** `prod-sa-east`.
- **tiles-svc:** `prod-sa-east`, `prod-ap-south`, `prod-eu-west` and `prod-au-east`.

**Earliest times for the rest (UTC)**
- **geo-api:**
  - `prod-au-east`: Nov 2 14:00
  - `prod-us-east`: Nov 3 03:00
  - `prod-eu-central`: Nov 3 05:00
  - `prod-us-west`: Nov 4 07:00
  - `prod-ap-east`: Nov 4 17:00
- **relay-svc:**
  - `prod-ap-south`: Nov 2 20:30
  - `prod-au-east`: Nov 3 14:00
  - `prod-us-east`: Nov 4 03:00
  - `prod-eu-central`: Nov 4 05:00
  - `prod-ap-east`: Nov 4 17:00
  - `prod-us-west`: Nov 5 07:00
- **tiles-svc:**
  - `prod-eu-central`: Nov 3 05:00
  - `prod-us-west`: Nov 4 07:00
  - `prod-ap-east`: Nov 4 17:00

**What drove the times**
- **Blackouts:** the active `prod-eu-central` blackout on Nov 2 and the `prod-ap-east` blackout on Nov 4 pushed those regions later.
- **Rollback:** geo-api `prod-ap-south` was rolled back and redeployed, so its bake time counts from the new deployment on Nov 1 at 21:35.

I only deployed the three plan services (geo-api, relay-svc and tiles-svc), and only to the two regions above. I didn't touch `search-api`, which isn't in the plan, or staging. I used the current plan, runbook revision 4 and the current calendars, not the superseded draft plan.

The output is in `/app/rollout-2026.11.json`, and `/app/STATUS.json` is marked success.
